symbols.note: Set to 120_000; used as cap for B arm token count in eval_task_arms

symbols.note: Deterministic A/B/C comparison for one task; returns dict with recall and token counts

claims.text: A = the distilled semantic slice (today's product).
claims.why: The chunk does not define 'semantic slice' or verify it is the product; only calls semantic_slice and uses res['slice_text']

claims.text: B = naive whole-repo concat. Recall is measured against the TRUE, FULL, UNTRUNCATED text (``tokens_B``) -- beating a baseline you truncated is not a win.
claims.why: The chunk shows text_b_full is obtained via _whole_repo_text with cap_chars=None, but the function _whole_repo_text is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify it returns full untruncated text

claims.text: ``tokens_B_capped_at_default``/``b_truncated_at_cap`` additionally report what Tier 2 would actually hand a model (capped at ``_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS``), so that weakening is visible, not hidden inside a smaller B that looks stronger than it is.
claims.why: The code computes text_b_capped with cap_chars=_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS*4, and returns tokens_B_capped_at_default and b_truncated_at_cap from _whole_repo_text (second return value). The claim matches the implementation.

claims.text: C = BM25 top-k retrieval, budgeted to the SAME token count as A (``token_budget_C == tokens_A``) -- the 'dumb retrieval' baseline that matters commercially.
claims.why: Code sets budget_c = max(tokens_a, 1) and passes it as budget_tokens to _bm25_context; token_budget_C is returned as budget_c. Claim matches.

claims.text: ``c_beats_a`` is TIE-INCLUSIVE (``recall_C >= recall_A``, matching the report's 'C>=A' column and this module's own docstring promise that a tie is 'reported loudly, not smoothed over') and reported plainly either way; nothing here is tuned to make A win.
claims.why: The return dict sets 'c_beats_a': recall_c >= recall_a, which is tie-inclusive. The docstring comment explains the rationale.

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: same per-task resolution guard as ``eval_task_tier1`` -- a ``ValueError``/``OSError`` resolving the repo or slicing the target returns an ERRORED row (``_task_error_row``) instead of propagating.
claims.why: The code wraps the resolution and slicing in a try-except catching ValueError and OSError, returning _task_error_row(task, exc).

claims.text: A CORRECTNESS task is likewise refused (``_correctness_task_row``) rather than scored: all three arms here go through ``_recall``, so a task with no ``must_include`` would read as a perfect 1.0 in every arm at once.
claims.why: The code checks is_correctness_task(task) and returns _correctness_task_row(task) early.
The chunk does not define or verify what 'the product' is; only assigns text_a = res['slice_text']
The function _whole_repo_text is not defined in this chunk; cannot confirm it concatenates the whole repo naively.

claims.text: Recall is measured against the TRUE, FULL, UNTRUNCATED text
claims.why: The chunk shows _recall(text_b_full, must_include) but _recall definition is not in this chunk; cannot verify it measures recall against full text.
The function _bm25_context is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify it uses BM25 or top-k retrieval.

claims.text: A tie is 'reported loudly, not smoothed over'
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the report module or the docstring referenced; only shows the tie-inclusive comparison.

claims.why: No evidence in chunk about tuning; the comparison is deterministic and tie-inclusive, but intent cannot be verified from code alone.

observations.what: eval_task_arms uses _whole_repo_text with cap_chars=None for B, and cap_chars=_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS*4 for capped version; the multiplier 4 is undocumented and appears in the code but not in the docstring.
The function run_arms is declared but its body is not included in this chunk; the docstring claims default tasks but cannot be verified.
The claim 'NEVER RAISES' is only partially true; only ValueError and OSError are caught. Other exceptions (e.g., from _bm25_context, _recall) could propagate.
